target_customer: Businesses and recruitment teams that want employees to have a business number in an app on their personal phone
problem: SaaS VoIP providers lease numbers from carriers and pass on connection and usage costs; businesses want cheaper business numbers on personal phones with analytics and integrations.
business_model: Per-user monthly subscription (YC page says about $20 per user per month; website now lists GBP 30 and 39 plans)
product_category: Business phone system and mobile network for business (VoIP)

founders.name: Nick Browne
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; education not listed.

founders.name: Edward Clayton
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; C# developer, mostly in finance.

founders.name: Leo Bartle
founders.background_notes: YC launch post calls him an increasingly active co-founder who owns the UK mobile network Devyce works with; Tech.eu body text also names him a co-founder.

competitors.name: OpenPhone
competitors.what: Business phone number in an app, YC backed

competitors.name: Dialpad
competitors.what: Cloud business communications aimed at larger companies
competitors.funding_then: $165M at a $1.2B valuation reported in late 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: VoIP apps are standard engineering, but owning a mobile network operator relationship adds telecom integration and regulatory complexity.

defensibility.rationale: Affiliation with a UK mobile network operator gives cheaper numbers than leasing VoIP providers, a structural cost advantage claimed by the company.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; incumbents kept competing as software VoIP providers.

market_need_then: Hybrid work after 2020 raised demand for business numbers on personal phones; Tech.eu cites savings of up to 70 percent versus leasing models, a company claim.

branding.domain_note: Uses devyce.com; no acquisition history found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is a misspelled device; no press on the brand itself or community evidence found.

pivots.from: Business phone numbers for all businesses with the aim of becoming a mobile network
pivots.to: VoIP phone system focused on recruitment teams (current website)
pivots.why: Not stated by sources; inferred only from the current website positioning, so date is null.

outcome_analysis: Devyce raised a $2.7M seed in February 2023 after YC and appears operating with a recruitment-focused product and public pricing. No shutdown or acquisition was found. Its structural cost edge comes from the sister mobile operator, but traction numbers are not public so the outcome is still open.
notes: Seed reported by three outlets in different currencies (Tech.eu $2.7M, EU-Startups EUR 2.5M, Bdaily GBP 2.2M). Aggregators show other totals ($4.2M, $2.82M, a $5M undated item) that are unverified. Tech.eu inconsistently names co-founders.
